options: Can I help you? I'll hold the bike.
I have to go now. I'll call you later.
How long will it take? I'm busy right now.
I want to learn how to fix it. It looks interesting.
Can you fix my bike, too? Thank you for your help.
questions.question:
G: Hey, Junsu. What are you doing?
B: Hi, Amy. There is a problem with my bike. I'm trying to fix it.
G: ______________________________
B: Sure, thank you.

빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
questions.explanation: B가 'Sure, thank you.'라고 답한 것으로 보아, G의 대사는 도움을 제안하는 표현이어야 한다. 'Can I help you?'는 자연스러운 도움 제안 표현이다.

options: Rules for Using the Cafeteria
How to Make Students Happier
The Difficulties of Team Projects
The Importance of Reducing Waste
Warm Hearts: A School Problem Solver
questions.question:
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?"

The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem. We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food.

Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success! The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste!

글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: Warm Hearts 동아리가 식사 낭비 문제를 해결한 과정을 설명하는 글이다. 동아리가 학교 문제를 해결하는 주체가 되며, 이것이 글의 중심 내용이다.

options: We know how to use digital kiosks.
Not everyone thinks digital kiosks are easy.
The class was held at the community center.
You can choose from the menu after paying.
People felt more comfortable with kiosks after the class.
questions.question:
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks.

To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.

After the class, people said, "Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.explanation: 글에서 'starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying'의 순서로 설명하고 있으므로, 메뉴를 고르는 것은 결제 전이다. 따라서 '결제 후에 메뉴를 고를 수 있다'는 틀린 내용이다.

questions.question:
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to ⓐ look for problems in our community. We ⓑ found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads needed ⓒ more lights. With the help of a teacher, we ⓓ put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel ⓔ more dangerous than before!

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: 문맥상 이웃들이 더 안전함을 느껴야 하는데, 'more dangerous'라고 표현하면 더 위험하다는 뜻이 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. 'more safe'나 'safer'가 되어야 한다.

options: No problem.
It's nothing.
My pleasure.
That's too bad.
Don't mention it.
questions.question:
G: Jack, those boxes look heavy. Can I help you?
B: Yes, please. Can you take this one?
G: No problem.
B: Thank you for carrying it.
G: You're welcome.

밑줄 친 부분과 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
questions.explanation: 'That's too bad'는 '그건 안됐네' 또는 '안타깝다'는 부정적인 의미이므로, 감사의 말에 대한 응답으로 적절하지 않다. 나머지는 모두 '괜찮다', '도와줄 수 있어서 기쁘다'는 긍정적인 반응을 나타낸다.

options: Good ideas can be easily forgotten.
Finding a solution takes a very long time.
Even the smallest acts can make a big difference!
Ignoring small issues causes serious problems later.
Speaking in front of many people makes you feel uncomfortable.
questions.question:

글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.explanation: 글은 작은 봉사 활동이 사람들에게 도움을 주고 변화를 만들었다는 내용이다. 따라서 '가장 작은 행동도 큰 차이를 만들 수 있다'는 결론이 가장 적절하다.

options: the best tools for solving community problems
the importance of volunteering for all students
the future goals of Warm Hearts club members
how Yuna felt when she became the club leader
some cases of Warm Hearts solving school and community problems
questions.question:
Hello, everyone! I'm Yuna, and I'm the leader of Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has solved some problems in our school and our community over the past few years. I want to share our stories.

다음 글에 이어질 내용으로 알맞은 것은?
questions.explanation: Yuna가 '우리 이야기를 나누고 싶다'고 했으므로, 다음에는 Warm Hearts가 해결한 실제 사례들이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

options: community: the people living in a particular area
gather: to join other people somewhere to make a group
comfortable: making you feel relaxed and free from pain
reduce: to find the answer to something or to stop a problem
announce: to tell people new information, especially officially
questions.question: 다음 중 영영 풀이가 잘못 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: 'reduce'는 '줄이다', '감소시키다'라는 의미인데, 'to find the answer to something'은 'solve'의 뜻이다. reduce의 정확한 의미는 'to make something smaller in size or amount'이다.

questions.question:
Volunteering can be a great experience. ⓐ I have volunteered at the local library before. ⓑ I read English books to kids who were not good at English. ⓒ The library has strict rules about returning books on time. ⓓ The most meaningful moment for me was seeing the smiles on the kids' faces. ⓔ After volunteering, I felt happier because I was able to help many kids.

다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.explanation: 글은 도서관에서의 봉사 경험과 그로 인한 의미 있는 순간들을 설명한다. ⓒ는 도서관의 일반적인 규칙에 대한 내용으로, 개인의 봉사 경험과 무관하므로 전체 흐름을 방해한다.

questions.question:
B: Hello, Ms. Lee. Can I help you? Your hands are full.
ⓐ Okay. Is there anything else?
ⓑ Thank you! Please put them over there.
ⓒ That's it. Thank you so much for helping me.
ⓓ Oh, hi, Jihun. Yes, please. Can you open the door for me?
ⓔ No problem. I can also carry the books for you.
ⓕ You're welcome. Have a nice day, Ms. Lee!

대화의 흐름이 자연스럽도록 ⓐ~ⓔ를 순서대로 바르게 배열한 것은?
questions.explanation: 자연스러운 순서: ⓓ(인사 및 도움 요청) → ⓔ(추가 도움 제안) → ⓑ(감사 및 지시) → ⓐ(더 필요한 것 확인) → ⓒ(감사) → ⓕ(인사말)

options: Has you visit China before?
Have you visit China before?
Has you visited China before?
Have you visited China before?
Have you visiting China before?
questions.question:
주어진 우리말을 영어로 알맞게 옮긴 것은?

너는 중국에 방문해 본 적이 있니?
questions.explanation: 현재완료 형태로 '~한 적이 있니?'는 'Have you (ever) visited...?'로 표현된다. you는 2인칭이므로 'have'를 사용하고, 동사는 과거분사 'visited'를 사용해야 한다.

questions.question:
After we solved this problem at our school, we started ⓐ to look for problems in our community. We found out ⓑ that some roads around our school ⓒ was very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. ⓓ With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel ⓔ more safe than before!

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 모두 고르시오.
questions.explanation: ⓒ에서 주어 'roads'는 복수형이므로 'was'가 아닌 'were'를 사용해야 한다. ⓔ에서 'safe'는 일음절 형용사이므로 'more safe'가 아닌 'safer'를 사용해야 한다. 따라서 ⓒ와 ⓔ가 틀렸다.

options: I have visited Japan twice.
Jackson has never ridden a bike.
She has lived in the house for 3 years.
I have never gotten a love letter before.
John and Mike have eaten a crab before.
questions.question: 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ①④⑤는 과거의 특정 시점의 경험을 나타내고, ②는 과거부터 현재까지의 부정을 나타낸다. ③은 '3년 동안 살고 있다'는 과거부터 현재까지 지속되는 상황을 나타내므로 다르다.

options: use / comfortabler
used / comfortabler
used / more comfortable
using / more comfortable
using / most comfortable
questions.question:
Have you ever ⓐ__________ a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks.

To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.

After the class, people said, "Now we feel ⓑ __________ with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 현재완료 형태이므로 과거분사 'used'가 필요하다. ⓑ는 비교 표현으로 'more comfortable'(더 편안한)이 적절하다. 'comfortable'은 다음절 형용사이므로 'more'를 붙여야 한다.

options: Mina is shorter ______ Amy.
John runs faster ______ his friends.
She is more famous ______ her sister.
Sora looks more beautiful ______ others.
This is the biggest animal ______ the world.
questions.question: 다음 중 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ①②③④는 모두 비교 표현으로 'than'이 들어간다. 하지만 ⑤는 최상급 표현으로 'in the world'가 들어가야 한다.
